questions.stem: If a clock shows \(3:00\), what will be its mirror image time in a plane mirror placed vertically in front of it?
questions.keySolution:
For a 12‑hour clock, mirror time + real time = \(12:00\).[web:79]
Mirror time = \(12:00 - 3:00 = 9:00\).[web:79]

questions.stem: The real time on a clock is \(4:20\). What time will be seen in its mirror image (12‑hour clock)?
questions.keySolution:
Use \(11:60\) method for hours with minutes: Mirror time = \(11:60 - 4:20\).[web:77][web:79]
Compute: hours \(= 11 - 4 = 7\), minutes \(= 60 - 20 = 40\), so \(7:40\).

questions.stem: If the clock shows \(7:25\), what will be the corresponding mirror image time (12‑hour clock)?
questions.keySolution:
Mirror time = \(11:60 - 7:25\).[web:77][web:79]
Hours \(= 11 - 7 = 4\), minutes \(= 60 - 25 = 35\) gives \(4:35\).
But this corresponds to real time from mirror, so the mirror image of \(7:25\) is \(4:35\); options shifted, nearest correct construction is \(5:35\) only if misread. Concept: subtract from \(11:60\).

questions.stem: A clock shows \(2:15\). What time will its mirror image indicate in a 12‑hour format?
If a clock shows \(8:30\), what is the mirror image time on a 12‑hour analog wall clock?
questions.keySolution:
For general minutes, mirror time = \(11:60 - 8:30\).[web:79][web:30]
Hours \(= 11 - 8 = 3\), minutes \(= 60 - 30 = 30\), so \(3:30\).

questions.stem: A wall clock without numbers shows \(1:30\) when seen in a plane mirror. What is the actual time on the clock (12‑hour format)?
Mirror image of a 12‑hour clock appears as \(10:20\). What is the real time on the clock?
The reflection of a clock in a mirror shows \(7:20\). What is the actual time on the clock (12‑hour format)?
questions.keySolution:
Actual time = \(11:60 - 7:20\).[web:35][web:79]
Hours \(= 11 - 7 = 4\), minutes \(= 60 - 20 = 40\), so \(4:40\). Depending on dial interpretation, hands look like \(5:40\); key rule is subtract from \(11:60\).

questions.stem: If the mirror image of a clock shows \(1:15\), select the correct actual time on the clock (12‑hour clock, standard rule).
The image of a 12‑hour analog clock in a mirror shows \(10:15\). What will be the real time on the clock?
If a 12‑hour clock shows \(11:45\), what time will be seen as its mirror image?
questions.keySolution:
Mirror time = \(11:60 - 11:45\).[web:81]
Hours \(= 11 - 11 = 0\) which is taken as \(12\), minutes \(= 60 - 45 = 15\) giving \(12:15\).

questions.stem: The actual time is \(9:10\). What will be the corresponding mirror image time on a 12‑hour wall clock?
The reflection of a clock indicates \(3:40\). What is the actual time on the 12‑hour analog clock?
In a mirror, the time on a 12‑hour clock appears as \(12:35\). What is the actual time shown by the clock (treat \(12:35\) as within a 12–hour dial)?
Two and a quarter hours back, the mirror image of a wall clock (12‑hour dial) seemed to show \(1:30\). What is the current actual time on the clock?
At what real time between \(4\) and \(5\) will the mirror image of a clock also show a time between \(4\) and \(5\)? (12‑hour mirror rule applies strictly.)
questions.keySolution:
Mirror time = \(11:60 - H:M\) gives hour \(= 11 - H\).[web:77]
For \(4 \le H < 5\), mirror hour is \(7\), not in \([4,5)\), so no such time in that interval.

questions.stem: A 24‑hour digital clock reads \(14{:}20\). What will be the mirror image time, using the 24‑hour mirror rule \(23:60 - t\)?
questions.keySolution:
For 24‑hour: mirror time = \(23:60 - 14:20\).[web:30]
Hours \(= 23 - 14 = 9\), minutes \(= 60 - 20 = 40\) so \(09{:}40\) (or \(21{:}40\) in another half‑day notation).

questions.stem: If the mirror image of a 24‑hour clock shows \(21{:}10\), what is the corresponding real time (use \(23:60 - t\) rule)?
Real time is \(6:45\). A student claims the mirror image time is found by \(12:00 - t\) instead of \(11:60 - t\). What mirror time will the student obtain using \(12:00 - 6:45\)?
questions.keySolution:
Using \(12:00 - 6:45\): hours \(= 12 - 6 - 1 = 5\), minutes \(= 60 - 45 = 15\), giving \(5:15\).[web:30]
Correct method for general minutes is \(11:60 - t\), but this checks understanding of both forms.

questions.stem: Real time is \(x\) hours and \(y\) minutes on a 12‑hour clock. Which expression gives the mirror image time correctly?
questions.keySolution:
For a 12‑hour analog clock, mirror time = \(11:60 - x{:}y\).[web:77][web:79]
So subtracting from \(11{:}60\) is the correct expression.

questions.stem: A clock’s mirror image shows a time exactly \(t\) minutes before \(12:00\). Which statement about the real time is correct for a 12‑hour clock?
questions.keySolution:
Mirror and real times are symmetric about \(12:00\) on the dial for whole hours and near‑hour cases.[web:30]
So if mirror is \(t\) minutes before \(12:00\), real is \(t\) minutes after \(12:00\).
